No capsule, no balloon: the ³He in the beam sets the rate, and a 1 bar balloon holds ×30 less of it. What floods the detector is the room and the shield wall, not the target.

thin target: captures/s = N(³He in the beam) · φ · ⟨σ_nγ⟩; 2.8 MeV × 30 mA, cell centre 2 m from the Li, no Pb

φ = 1.4×10⁸ n/cm²/s at 2 m, ⟨σ_nγ⟩ = 53 µb, ⟨α⟩ = 4.7×10⁻³ pairs per capture. A 1 bar balloon needs ×30 the volume of the 30 bar cell for the same rate — and a ×30 wider beam through the apparatus. The capsule needs a Ø2 cm beam but has 1 % X₀ of walls. Nothing from n_TOF is in hand: every option buys its ³He (2.5 k€/L, he4_bag).

3

Every capture comes with ~36 000 neutrons scattered off the ³He itself

σ_el(³He, 0.5 MeV) ≈ 1.9 b against σ_nγ ≈ 53 µb: the load per X17 is the same for every target design

beam through the target region

30 bar cell, big slab: 8.6×10⁶ /s above 50 keVee (quenched proton recoils); capsule 6.3×10⁵, balloon R 5 3.9×10⁵.

it scales with the captures

Less ³He, less load — and less signal in the same ratio. A balloon buys nothing here; only the current (or the distance) trades load against rate.

The room term goes with the beam rate (beam area × flux), not with the ³He: the wide balloon (Ø18 cm beam) gets ×5 the 30 bar cell's room load for a fifth of its signal. Neutrons < 1.1 MeV never fire a leg directly: the legs are 2.2 MeV H-capture γ and concrete capture γ.

Mostly neutrons leaking through the wall (proton recoils, quenched). Not saturated in the sense of the PMT physics, but at gain 10⁶ the anode current is in the range where gain drifts; at 10⁵ it is 3 µA. The pile-up is in the reach (added to each arm's calorimetry): it moves the best E_sum cut up to 14 MeV.

Recoil protons from the isobutane and heavy recoils from argon: short, dense clusters. A charge / size cut should remove most; not modelled here. Most come through the wall (3×10⁵ /s per arm). Charged in full (e^(−2·occ)), the 30 bar cell needs 23 d instead of 6.7 d.

At the exit, 70 % of the collided neutrons are within 30 cm of the Ø8 cm bore: the halo scattered in the bore walls and the Pb plug, not bulk transmission. The ⁸Be γ that cross the exit plane mostly went round the wall through the 50 cm side walls of the model's target room (an artefact of the bunker model).

The wall decides: 5 cm of Pb on the exit is not enough; +10 cm Pb and +10 cm borated PE recover it

30 bar cell, big plastics, 30 mA; legs in the busiest arm from all sources; DREAM pair trigger only

shield walllegs /stwo-arm triggers /sDREAM liveMM occupancydays to ATOMKI
20 BPE + 80 concrete + 5 Pb (as first modelled)211,7005,63137%1.1928 d
+ 10 cm Pb on the exit93,2001,78965%0.7412 d
+ 10 cm Pb + 10 cm borated PE (headline)37,67061684%0.596.7 d

Pb kills the capture γ of the concrete (hard: 60 % above 1.5 MeV, lines up to 10 MeV): legs ×33 down. Borated PE kills the slow neutrons that make capture γ inside the detector: legs ×9 down. The two exit layers were simulated one at a time from the same exit phase space; the headline combines them (photons behind the Pb, neutrons behind the PE), an estimate.

12

What to do with this

1. Target: the 30 bar Be/CFRP cell (or as much ³He as the budget allows, as dense as walls permit). The balloon and the capsule are both worse per euro of ³He; the capsule is not available anyway.

2. Beam dump far away and lined (⁶Li / borated PE), the experimental room lined; the dump decides the trigger load.

3. A stepped collimator with a borated / ⁶Li liner instead of a straight Ø8 cm bore.

4. Pair trigger only on DREAM; cosmic calibration in separate runs.

5. Bench test: MM cluster cut against neutron recoils (AmBe or a D-D source).

6. Ask Birmingham: room layout, wall thickness, where a dump could go.
